uniequip_002_haak:
Rain's lifted, but night's just in time to sweep in again. This makes how many times I've slammed the door and left?
Hung's some kind of insufferable dude, for real. Keeps dragging me into arguments over 'the meaning of medicine' and 'the right track' and 'having a responsibility.' Like all of that isn't just phony self-servicing junk.
The market ain't no peaceful place, but at least it ain't noise that cares about me. Besides, it's not like I'm a stranger to life here. Just reliving the good old days on the lam with the old sleazebag, am I right?
'Thief! C-Catch him!'
Man, every day they put on the same dull crap. I'll hand it to the tourist though, a guy with no strength in his right arm stealin' your bag's pretty hilarious. And hopeless.
Actually, check that out, I think the thief's a familiar face? That's the poor sucker who came to me for a detox in the middle of the night. He had his whole gang carryin' him around like a swollen eggplant hopped up on growth hormones.
Looks like I went a little too easy on him. Man, I knew letting the poison wreck his left arm more would've been a good idea.
I've said it before, medicine's not gonna stop harm at the source. If Hung thinks he's so smart...
'*sob* Grampa...'
Yo, hassle just keeps findin' me. Don't you dare look my way.
'D... Doctor? You have to save my grampa, he's my only family...
'Save how? The old man's practically counting the days. Maybe someone can lay him in a nice sandalwood coffin, give him a decent exit. Either way, that someone ain't me.
Think it was a night like this one too, just after the rain lifted. My pops was down for the count after takin' a stray bullet. He dragged me to hide in some street corner he found. Dude hoped I'd take on his mantle. Maybe relieve his pain, or... just straight up address it.
The way he went out was kinda ridiculous. Rememberin' how he loved to own the whole unlicensed doctor thing just makes it funnier.
'*sob*...'
Screw it, I gotta do somethin' to make this kid quit crying so ugly.
We'll take watermelon, lychee, and pineapple flavor, mix 'em up, squeeze out the bubbles, aaand... perfect, this med's gonna please the crowd like nothin' else.
C'mon, old timer, give your grandkid some peace of mind. Lemme jab you up nice and good.
'Huh? Grampa, are you awake? Grampa? Doctor, why is my grampa laughing so hard...? Grampa, stop laughing, you're gonna make me laugh too...'
Hey, a few side-effects comes with the territory. Also, never call me a doctor again, or I'll tell you straight to your face that even if he lasts the night, he—
Whatever, <i>at least he can last the night.
......
'Cooking skills won't stop starvation at the source either. Are you saying that's pointless too?'
Weird. How come Hung preaching at me just flashed through my brain? Yeuch, guess I'm gettin' a little peckish, though...
Huh? The kitchen lights are still on... dude, Hung, did you not go to bed yet?
'Here, your midnight snack.
'After you're done, wash the dishes, then put them back in the cupboard. They're good habits to learn.'
The hell? Here he goes again, educating people without asking.
uniequip_003_haak:
'If you still want to keep that arm, sit tight and quit squirming.'
Scolded into silence, the Logistics operator sat back down on the bench, ill at ease. If not for his injury... he would never have come to Aak for help.
'Remind me again, how'd you get hurt?'
'I took a fall while helping Engineering train their newly developed combat robot.'
'And how does taking a fall put a steel pin this long inside your arm?'
'It didn't get driven in.' The operator's voice grew smaller and smaller. 'Medical implanted it during surgery last week.'
'Huh?'
'Fracture surgery. Same arm, same reason.' The operator scratched his head. 'Please don't tell anyone. Nobody takes a beating from a robot lying down.'
Aak let out two exaggerated laughs.
'All right, let's get started. This might sting a bit.'
'Wait, I'm not rea—Aaagh!'
The operator's eyes searched the room back and forth, trying to find something to take his mind off it. Then he spotted a battered notebook lying open on the table, the handwriting on it as frenzied as an incantation:
'A hundred poisons, boiled down till not a dreg remains. Take the clear liquid, and keep it from light and heat.'
Aak drew a vial of deep blue liquid out of his thermos.
'Three inches from the vessel of the heart, inject.'
Aak drove the needle down hard.
'Draw blood, and the throat is sealed!'
'Hold on—' the operator roared, cold sweat pouring off him like rain.
Aak clicked his tongue and stuffed a towel into his mouth.
When the operator came to again, all that remained where the wound had been was a faint line of stitches.
Aak spoke at his leisure. 'Run it the other way, block the nerve conduction, halve the dose, and death turns into life.'
'Th-That notebook?' The operator looked back at the table, but the notebook was nowhere to be seen.
'Oh, that's actually a ledger. Who owes whose life, who wants to kill who, how they'll do it, it's all written down nice and clear. Shame everyone named in it, and the guy who wrote it, are all dead.'
'Then my arm...'
'It's fine. While I was in there I boosted the explosive power of every muscle in your body, so that robot doesn't stand a chance against you now.' Aak said. 'Course, when I say every muscle, that includes tissue like the diaphragm.'
'What—hic—what does that mean?'
'It means you'll be hiccupping nonstop, just like that, for two or three weeks straight. Hah! If you don't like hiccups, I can always think of something else. Oh right, would you rather have intestinal gas venting itself uncontrollably from somewhere else instead?'
Before he had even finished, the patient had already fled in a hiccupping panic. Aak patted the pocket of his coat, where the remnant scroll left behind by the Poison Doctor now lay quietly.
He seemed to be talking to himself, and also to be explaining slowly to someone, with a patience rarely seen in him:
'The old sleazebag figured that as long as he had dirt on all those people, he'd live a long life. And how'd that turn out? He died uglier than anyone.
'Me, I'm different. Whether I patch 'em up or break 'em for fun is all down to my mood. The only use this book has is for doodling in. Oh, right, and for reminding me not to live as exhaustingly as he did.'
